🔊 Exclusive | Iranian Navy carried out more than 20 operations against US warships: Commander

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Naval forces of the Iranian Army carried out more than 20 operations against US warships during the 40-day conflict that began on February 28, while approximately 300 additional operations targeted American interests in various locations, including through missile and drone strikes, the coordinating deputy of the Islamic Republic of Iran Army Navy has said.

In an exclusive interview with IRNA published on Thursday Rear Admiral Jalil Moghadam said that the operations demonstrated the Navy’s continued capabilities, rejecting US claims that Iran’s naval forces had been destroyed. He said American and Israeli forces had avoided approaching Iran’s coastline, particularly the Strait of Hormuz, remaining hundreds of kilometers away.
​
According to Moghadam, the conflict had prompted a major review of the Navy’s military doctrine. Lessons from the 12-day and 40-day wars were assessed, leading to revisions in operational priorities and equipment development, he said, adding that the proposals have been submitted to higher headquarters for review and approval.
​
He also elaborated on operations against US vessels, including the aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln. He noted that Iranian forces identified the carrier during the opening days of the conflict and targeted it with a strategic cruise missile. He said the carrier subsequently suspended flight operations for three days before moving away from Iran’s coast.
​
In another operation, he said, Iranian forces used drones, cruise missiles and electronic warfare systems against a US destroyer identified as DDG 103 after it harassed Iranian commercial and oil tankers. He added that three other US destroyers attempting to enter the Strait of Hormuz were targeted in a combined attack.
​
Moghadam said Iran’s naval capabilities and equipment had improved since the 40-day conflict and warned that any future confrontation would see broader operations.
​
He also said the Navy would continue pursuing accountability for the targeting of Iranian naval personnel, including those killed in earlier confrontations with US forces.
​
He added that Iran’s Armed Forces remained prepared for possible renewed conflict, regardless of diplomatic developments.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Three oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking sea mines while attempting to navigate an unauthorized route south of the Strait of Hormuz, the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) Navy has announced.

According to a statement published on the IRGC’s website on Thursday, the incidents occurred over the past 24 hours, leaving the tankers stranded along the southern coast of the strategic waterway.
​
The statement said the vessels had switched off all their radar and navigation systems and ignored warnings from the IRGC Navy as they attempted to leave through the unauthorized southern route.
​
The IRGC Navy warned that the route was contaminated with mines, holding the vessels’ owners and crews responsible for using it. It also urged them not to rely on “illusions” promoted by US Central Command (CENTCOM) on social media.
